text: In short, take care to make as many personal friends, and as few personal enemies, as possible. I do not mean, by personal friends, intimate and confidential friends, of which no man can hope to have half a dozen in the whole course of his life; but I mean friends, in the common acceptation of the word; that is, people who speak well of you, and who would rather do you good than harm, consistently with their own interest, and no further.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXXIX, to his son, London, August 28, Old Style 1751
